body: [P2] Use the host fetch signature instead of the DOM-only RequestInfo type. Reproduction on Node 24.18.0 / TypeScript 5.9.3: `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit --target ES2022 --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --strict --skipLibCheck --allowImportingTsExtensions --lib ES2022 --types node tests/market-fetch.spec.ts` fails with TS2552 at 15:37. This matches the repository's Node-only lib/types environment; adding DOM would hide the mismatch. Please use `input: Parameters<typeof globalThis.fetch>[0]` (which already includes string/URL/Request). I verified that one-line change makes the explicit typecheck pass and keeps all 16 tests passing. The existing npm typecheck does not catch this because it excludes tests.

Non-blocking test-strength follow-up: this regex verifies the HTTP status prefix but not the claimed 200-character truncation. A temporary local mutation replacing `body.slice(0, 200)` with the full body still passed all 41 market tests. Consider asserting the complete message suffix/length. Separately, the native report's uncovered market.ts lines 223-224 and 226-228 are the shared safeFetch network/HTTP paths used by the other five providers; adding one representative OKX rejection/non-2xx case would cover those without a production refactor. A local mutation losing safeFetch's error context also survived all 41 tests. These are coverage-strength opportunities, not a rejection of the verified >=85% line result.
